chunks: From him, from Moalla, from Al-Washa, from Abdul-Kareem ibn Amr Al-Khasha'i, from Umar ibn Hanzala, and from Hamza ibn Humran, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, this world, Allah gives it to the righteous and the immoral, and He does not give faith except to His choicest ones from His creation.
ai.seo_question: Does Allah give the world to both good and bad people?
ai.summary: In Shia theology, this narration from al-Kafi underscores the divine wisdom behind the indiscriminate distribution of worldly blessings, which serve as a test for all humanity, while true faith (Iman) is reserved as a special grace for the 'safwah' (elite). This distinction highlights that material prosperity is not a sign of divine favor, whereas spiritual election is a selective bestowal by Allah. The hadith reinforces the concept that the path to salvation requires divine guidance rather than mere worldly success.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Moalla, from Al Washa, from Abdul Kareem Bin Amro Al Khash’amy, from Umar Bin Hanzala, and from Haza Bin Humran, from Humran, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘This world, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Gives it to the righteous and the immoral, and (but) He<sup>azwj</sup> does not Give the Eman except to His<sup>azwj</sup> from His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Mu’alla from al- Washsha’ from ‘Abd al-Karim ibn ‘Amr al-Khath’ami from ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah and Hamza ibn Humran from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Allah gives this world to both the virtuous and evil-doing people, but He does not give belief to anyone except to His chosen creatures.”
